card.title: PROTECTED CONVOY
card.text: Add a PRODUCTION and a PLAN to your hand.
card.flavorText: During WWII, British and Allied convoys transported essential supplies such as food, fuel, and equipment across oceans. These groups of merchant ships, escorted by warships, faced constant threats from German U-boats, aircraft, and surface raiders. Convoys operated in key regions such as the North Atlantic, Arctic, and Mediterranean, where they ensured the flow of essential resources to Allied forces and civilian populations. To counter attacks, convoys relied heavily on coordinated tactics. Escort ships used sonar and depth charges to detect and engage submarines. Aircraft patrols, including long-range bombers, reduced U-boat effectiveness by forcing them to submerge. Intelligence from decoded German communications (designated Ultra) allowed convoys to reroute away from U-boat "wolf packs". New weapons such as the Hedgehog mortar improved anti-submarine accuracy, and decoy ships, disguised as civilian vessels, lured U-boats into range of hidden guns. By 1943, improved technology, air coverage, and convoy organization significantly reduced losses. These measures, combined with Allied industrial production and codebreaking, secured Allied control of sea routes by 1945.
